quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONNECTED SPEECH PHENOMENON IN THE PHRASE
quests.hint: The final /d/ in 'could' runs straight into the /j/ sound that starts 'yield'. What single new sound do they fuse into?
quests.explanation: When /d/ meets /j/ across a word boundary, the two sounds often fuse into a single new consonant. /d/ + /j/ merges into /dʒ/, so "could yield" sounds like the two words have melted together.
quests.phoneticRule: In fast speech, native speakers blend and drop sounds to speak more smoothly.
